Anya: noticing p95 jumps on model-zeta around 03:12 UTC, intermittent p99 > 900ms and throughput drop ~15%
Sam: saw the alerts, looks like continuous-batcher nodes on shard-7. Any recent releases?
Mike: no config rollouts in the last 48h. infra shows kernel_swap_count climbing and small microbatches more frequent.
Toni: paste recent kernel-selector log tail and any quick flame profile pls
Anya: log excerpt below, full logs uploaded to ticket
```
[03:12:07] kernel-selector: selected=quant_fast (cached)
[03:12:09] kernel-selector: selected=ref_stable (swap: seq_mix_mismatch)
[03:12:09] admission: microbatch_size=2 -> 1 (rapid shrink)
[03:12:10] kvcache: overall_hit=49% (baseline ~96% at 02:45)
[03:12:12] kernel-selector: selected=quant_fast (reinit)
```
Sam: that rapid select back-and-forth is suspicious. Could be mixed seq_len within batch triggering incompatible kernel choice. Also see tenant-73 bursty tiny sequences on same hosts.
Mike: grabbed a short perf dump (summary):
```
select_kernel()    39%  p99=13.5ms
admit_request()     30%  p99=8.2ms
kv_cache_lookup()   15%  p99=4.0ms
pack_batches()      10%  p99=5.8ms
```
profiling-bot: trace uploaded s3://redwood-profiles/2119987654/model-zeta/trace.pb
Toni: select_kernel p99 at 13ms is too high and explains latency tail. Why reinit so often? Are we seeing kernel binary eviction or small JIT patches?
Anya: hypothesis: adaptive-quant path prefers quant_fast for short sequences, but when a longer sequence enters the same batch (or cache miss forces full context), selector flips to ref_stable which triggers kernel reinit. Admission controller then shrinks microbatches to try to meet latency SLO, increasing chance of mixing short+long in new batches -> feedback loop. KV cache coldness from noisy tenant makes long requests behave as even longer (more KV misses) and increases mixing probability.
Sam: confirmed noisy tenant-73 spikes at same times. KV warmness drops cause more full-context work.
Mike: I put together a reproduction script to run on a dev node with a 80/20 mix of short/long requests + a background noisy-tenant emulator. Command:
```
./tools/loadgen --model model-zeta --mix "short:80,long:20" --background-noise tenant-73 --duration 10m --out /tmp/run.log
```
Mike: repro shows kernel_swap_count increases ~7x and p99 spikes mirror prod. Also observed kernel_init() calls in worker logs every few seconds.
Toni: short-term mitigation ideas:
- make selector prefer sticky kernel per worker while there are active in-flight batches (avoid flip for a few seconds)
- admission: require a stability window (e.g., 12s) before changing microbatch target aggressively
- selector: evaluate batch composition (ratio of long requests) instead of per-request seq_len threshold
Anya: I can run a 3-host canary with sticky-kernel=true and admission.stability_ms=12000. Also limit max_microbatch to 8 to avoid huge swings.
deploy-bot: canary rollout requested: cb-canary-3 -> hosts [cb-07, cb-09, cb-11]
Sam: after canary goes up (03:30) p95 fell ~40%, p99 down ~250ms, throughput back to -3% of baseline. KV hit_rate improved from ~50% -> ~85% on canary hosts. Kernel_swap_count dropped dramatically.
Mike: root-cause triage candidate: selector used absolute sequence-length cutoff and ignored kvcache warmness and batch composition. When kvcache hit_rate is low, effective processing cost per token changes and the selector misclassified which kernel would be optimal, causing many swaps. Admission control oscillation amplified mixing of sequence lengths.
Toni: proposed action items:
- ENG-4201: implement sticky kernel policy per-worker (short-term) -> assign Mike
- ENG-4202: enhance selector to consider batch composition and kvcache_hit_rate -> assign Sam
- ENG-4203: admission controller stability window and hysteresis on microbatch adjustments -> assign Anya
- perf-test: synthetic mixed-load + noisy-tenant overlay and track kernel_swap_count, kvcache_hit_rate, microbatch_hist
Anya: created ENG tickets and attached traces + loadgen recipe. Starting canary verification now, will keep thread updated.
Sam: also added temporary dashboard panels: eng-runtime/continuous-batcher -> kernel_swap_count / microbatch_hist / kvcache_hit_rate
Mike: I'll land a small sticky-kernel canary patch tomorrow morning, will capture post-patch profile for comparison.
Toni: make sure we collect per-worker kernel uptime metric and include in postmortem.
Anya: thanks all. keeping this thread open for 48h while patches and tests run. please post short updates. :coffee:
